name: Maximum Median
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ integers, where $$$n$$$ is odd. You can make the following operation with it: Choose one of the elements of the array (for example $$$a_i$$$) and increase it by $$$1$$$ (that is, replace it with $$$a_i + 1$$$). You want to make the median of the array the largest possible using at most $$$k$$$ operations. The median of the odd-sized array is the middle element after the array is sorted in non-decreasing order. For example, the median of the array $$$[1, 5, 2, 3, 5]$$$ is $$$3$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$n$$$ is odd, $$$1 \le k \le 10^9$$$) — the number of elements in the array and the largest number of operations you can make. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: Print a single integer — the maximum possible median after the operations.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1201C — Maximum Median [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
